reason: I'll start with the artery: its thick, elastic wall and inner lining seem suited to carrying blood away from the heart.
expectation: I expect the lining cells to form the inside of an artery, completing or advancing the artery goal.

alternatives.reason: I considered putting capillaries near cells to set up exchange, but chose to start with the outward route.
The vein also needs a lining, but I'll build the outward route first.

effect: The artery is complete, so I'll work on the exchange route next.
reaction: The smooth lining and outward arrows made the artery's role clear.
reason: Capillaries are thin and close to body cells, which seems important for exchanging materials.
expectation: I expect the capillaries to be positioned beside the cells, showing where oxygen and nutrients can reach them and carbon dioxide can leave.

alternatives.reason: The vein also needs its lining, but I want to build the exchange route before the return route.

effect: The capillary bed now shows exchange with nearby cells, so I can work on the return route.
reaction: It was useful to see that blood cells stay inside while dissolved materials cross.
reason: The venous wall needs a lining before the return route can be completed.
expectation: I expect a lined vein, probably still needing the one-way valve flaps.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the artery to the capillary bed also makes sense, but I want to prepare the vein first.

effect: The veins now have a lining and point back toward the heart; they still need valves.
reaction: The arrows make the return direction clear.
reason: I'll add the valve flaps to finish the return route goal.
expectation: I expect veins with valves that open for forward flow and close against backward flow.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the arteries to the capillary bed also makes sense, but I want to finish the veins first.

effect: The return route is ready, and the new goal is to join the three vessel routes.
reaction: Seeing muscle compression help push blood past the valves was useful.
reason: I'll connect the artery to the capillary bed first, following blood's outward route.
expectation: I expect the arteries to connect to the capillaries, leaving the veins to be joined afterward.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the capillaries to the veins also fits the goal, but I prefer to start at the outward end.

effect: The artery now connects to the capillaries, with the return side still open.
reaction: The branching picture makes the route easy to follow.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should complete the route back through the veins.
expectation: I expect the venous return to join the capillary bed, completing the three-part vessel route.

effect: The completed network connects the outward, exchange and return routes, finishing the chapter.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the whole route as one continuous path.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the capillary bed was most worthwhile: it showed what crosses between blood and nearby cells and what stays inside.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the lining to the vein felt least interesting because it was similar to lining the artery, even though the return direction was clear.

surprise.text: I didn't expect the picture to show a contracting muscle helping push blood through the veins while the valves prevent backward flow.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary; the pictures and goals gave each combination a purpose. The last connection was the only offered combination, though.

continue.text: Yes, I'd continue to see how the vessel network connects to the heart. Following blood's route made this chapter understandable, though some fittings were predictable.
